640a9b.title: Firestore Rules Open Access - Critical
640a9b.content:
Firestore security rules: `allow read, write: if true;` — ALL data publicly accessible and writable. The frontend uses Firebase client SDK directly, so these rules are the only server-side data access control. Found at /workspace/NepalCasts/NepalCasts/firestore.rules. This exposes all user PII (emails, phones), conversations, notifications, admin logs, etc. AND allows arbitrary writes — attackers can set isAdmin:true on their user doc to gain admin.

Storage rules also open: `allow read, write: if true;` at storage.rules.

b6d86c.title: Admin Privilege Escalation via Firestore - Critical
b6d86c.content:
Multiple admin checks rely on Firestore `isAdmin` or `admin` field that is directly writable by clients:
- Express `isAdmin` middleware checks `req.user?.admin === true` from JWT custom claims
- BUT Vercel API `verifyAdmin` (api/admin-users.js) checks Firestore `isAdmin` field: `userDoc.data()?.isAdmin !== true`
- Firestore rules allow `write: if true` so any authenticated (or even unauthenticated) user can set isAdmin:true on their user doc
- `bootstrapUserProfile` Firebase function hardcodes: `isAdmin: email === "aniltimilsena53@gmail.com"` — dev email gets admin
- `updateProfileByUid` writes unfiltered `...rest` to profiles doc (no server-side guard on sensitive fields)
